summary.executive_summary: This paper extends Mazur's theorem on the maximal unramified abelian covering of the modular curve X0(p) over Q. Mazur proved that the Shimura covering X2(p) → X0(p) is geometrically maximal, of degree Np := (p−1)/gcd(p−1,12). The authors show that the geometrically maximal abelian covering of X0(p) that is unramified outside the two cusps is strictly larger: it is a cyclic covering X′2(p) → X0(p) of degree 2Np. The construction proceeds by realizing Q(X′2(p)) as a quadratic extension of Q(X2(p)) generated by a square root of an explicitly built rational function Fh^2, where Fh is a product of generalized Dedekind eta functions. The transformation behavior of these functions under Γ0(p) is controlled via generalized eta functions Eg and the character ψ, and the ramification of Fh^2 is shown to occur precisely at the cusps with odd order. The main theorem (Theorem 1.2.2) states that the restriction of this covering to the affine curve Y0(p) = X0(p) minus the two cusps is geometrically maximal and unramified, and that the covering factors through the Shimura covering via a degree-two cover πp that is unramified outside cusps. The proof splits into the case p ≢ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) is a proper subgroup) and the case p ≡ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) = Γ1(p), requiring a triplet construction Gh). The result is a purely theoretical, proof-based note with no numerical experiments, datasets, or computational code. It contributes to the theory of unramified abelian extensions of function fields and to the arithmetic of modular curves, refining the understanding of how the maximal unramified covering relates to coverings that are allowed to ramify at the cusps.

Executive Summary
This paper extends Mazur's theorem on the maximal unramified abelian covering of the modular curve X0(p) over Q. Mazur proved that the Shimura covering X2(p) → X0(p) is geometrically maximal, of degree Np := (p−1)/gcd(p−1,12). The authors show that the geometrically maximal abelian covering of X0(p) that is unramified outside the two cusps is strictly larger: it is a cyclic covering X′2(p) → X0(p) of degree 2Np. The construction proceeds by realizing Q(X′2(p)) as a quadratic extension of Q(X2(p)) generated by a square root of an explicitly built rational function Fh^2, where Fh is a product of generalized Dedekind eta functions. The transformation behavior of these functions under Γ0(p) is controlled via generalized eta functions Eg and the character ψ, and the ramification of Fh^2 is shown to occur precisely at the cusps with odd order. The main theorem (Theorem 1.2.2) states that the restriction of this covering to the affine curve Y0(p) = X0(p) minus the two cusps is geometrically maximal and unramified, and that the covering factors through the Shimura covering via a degree-two cover πp that is unramified outside cusps. The proof splits into the case p ≢ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) is a proper subgroup) and the case p ≡ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) = Γ1(p), requiring a triplet construction Gh). The result is a purely theoretical, proof-based note with no numerical experiments, datasets, or computational code. It contributes to the theory of unramified abelian extensions of function fields and to the arithmetic of modular curves, refining the understanding of how the maximal unramified covering relates to coverings that are allowed to ramify at the cusps.

Research Context
Background on maximal unramified abelian coverings via fundamental groups. The maximal unramified abelian extension is governed by a finite group. Mazur's foundational result on the Shimura covering. The Shimura covering is geometrically maximal over Q. The degree of the Shimura covering is Np. The maximal unramified covering is a subcovering of X1(p) → X0(p).

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is the degree of the maximal unramified abelian covering of X0(p). Mazur's covering is maximal among unramified coverings, but the question is whether allowing ramification at cusps increases the degree. The hypothesis is that the maximal covering unramified outside cusps is cyclic of degree 2Np. The predicted outcome is that this covering factors through the Shimura covering via a degree-two cover. The degree-two cover is predicted to be unramified outside cusps. The construction is predicted to use generalized Dedekind eta functions.
